shots.title: One Hard Source
shots.brief: A single bare, small, hard light close to the subject. Let the shadow be ugly and sharp.
shots.constraint: One source, and it must be hard enough to throw a defined shadow.
shots.review: How far did the shadow travel, and did you fight it or use it?

shots.title: Leading Lines
shots.brief: Find lines in the space that point at your subject. Use all of them.
shots.constraint: At least two lines must converge on the subject.
shots.review: Do the lines actually point anywhere, or were you forcing it?

shots.title: Headroom
shots.brief: Same subject, five takes. Vary the space above their head from cramped to generous.
shots.constraint: Keep the head in frame in every take.
shots.review: At what point did extra headroom stop feeling like empty space and start feeling like intent?

shots.title: Thirds
shots.brief: Place your subject on a third line, horizontally and vertically. Both at once.
shots.constraint: Subject sits on an intersection of thirds lines.
shots.review: Did the rule help, or did you want to break it immediately?

shots.title: Full Manual
shots.brief: Shoot one shot with focus, exposure, and white balance all locked manually. Nothing auto.
shots.constraint: No auto anything, for one take.
shots.review: Which manual setting did you have to think hardest about?

shots.title: Pan Reveal
shots.brief: Start on something empty, pan across to the subject. The subject is not visible at the start.
shots.constraint: The reveal happens inside the take, not across a cut.
shots.review: Did the pan lead the eye, or did it feel like searching?

shots.title: Repetition With A Break
shots.brief: Frame a row of similar things. One of them is different. Compose so the break is the subject.
shots.constraint: The odd one out is the compositional anchor.
shots.review: Did the eye land on the break straight away, or did the pattern swallow it?

shots.title: Negative Space
shots.brief: Put a small subject in a big space. Let the frame breathe. The subject is under 20% of the image.
shots.constraint: The subject must occupy under a fifth of the frame.
shots.review: Is there a direction the subject is looking, and did the space agree with it?

shots.title: Tilt Up
shots.brief: Start framed on the ground. Tilt up to reveal what's above. One take, one movement.
shots.constraint: Start below the subject. Finish on it.
shots.review: What did the tilt reveal that justified the movement?

shots.title: One Subject, Three Sizes
shots.brief: Pick one subject and shoot it wide, medium, and tight from the same spot. Feet planted. Three separate shots, no moving.
shots.constraint: Do not move your feet between the three shots.
shots.review: Which of the three actually held attention? Was the tight one tighter than the subject deserves?

shots.title: Locked Off
shots.brief: Set the camera down and don't touch it. The subject moves through a 30 second static frame.
shots.constraint: Zero camera movement. If you touch it, start over.
shots.review: Did the static frame make the subject's movement more legible, or more boring?

shots.title: Practical Only
shots.brief: Light with whatever is already switched on in the room. A screen, a lamp, an indicator light. Nothing else.
shots.constraint: Only lights that are already on. You may not switch anything on.
shots.review: What was the source, and did you hide it or let it in frame?

shots.title: Texture Wall
shots.brief: Fill the entire frame with a single surface so you cannot tell what the object is. Get close.
shots.constraint: No horizon, no edges, no context. Surface only.
shots.review: Does it hold as an abstract image, or does it just look like an accident?

shots.title: Same Subject, Two Skies
shots.brief: Shoot the same subject in two lighting conditions. One with hard sun, one with flat cloud. Keep camera settings locked.
shots.constraint: Camera settings identical between the two shots.
shots.review: Which one needed less correction in post, and which one is the better shot?

shots.title: Four Corners
shots.brief: Same subject, same shot, four takes. Put the subject in each corner of the frame. No cropping to fix it.
shots.constraint: One take per corner, and you may not crop any of them.
shots.review: Which corner felt least awkward, and what was the frame doing on the other side?

shots.title: Symmetry
shots.brief: Find an axis of symmetry and shoot dead centre on it. Then shoot off that axis by a small amount.
shots.constraint: Both shots, same position in the space, only the alignment changes.
shots.review: Which one felt more deliberate, and why?

shots.title: Watch White Balance Drift
shots.brief: Lock white balance and shoot the same scene as the light changes. Watch it move.
shots.constraint: Manual white balance. No auto.
shots.review: What did the locked WB do to the colour as the light changed?

shots.title: Before And After
shots.brief: One object. Shoot it as it is, then change one thing, then shoot it again. Same frame, same light.
shots.constraint: Identical framing in both shots.
shots.review: Which single change carried the whole story?

shots.title: Pick A Shutter
shots.brief: Choose one shutter speed and ride it for five shots in different light. Change nothing else.
shots.constraint: Identical shutter speed across all five shots.
shots.review: At what point did the shutter become the problem instead of the tool?

shots.title: One Window
shots.brief: Light a subject with nothing but a single window. Turn off every other light in the room.
shots.constraint: One window. No artificial light at all.
shots.review: Which side of the face did you light, and did you notice the colour of the fill?

shots.title: Orbit
shots.brief: Arc around a still subject, roughly 45 degrees, in one take. The subject does not move.
shots.constraint: The subject stays completely still. Only you move.
shots.review: What did the new angle reveal that the start angle hid?
